page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-2 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance featuring 2 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, yielding an 8 GB per core memory-to-vCPU ratio. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor based on the x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates 1 physical core with 2 threads. The CPU includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It does not bundle local storage or GPU hardware, and includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, its multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25%, and Geekbench multi-core scores are in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth tests show weak to poor performance, with read-only small block cached bandwidth at 126.54 GB/sec (bottom 10%) and uncached large block write bandwidth at 22.01 GB/sec (bottom 25%). Single-threaded operations like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the n2d-highmem-2 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on dedicated AMD hardware, making it a viable entry point for memory-bound workloads that do not require heavy parallel processing. However, users face tradeoffs in multi-threaded throughput, database operations, and web serving, which all benchmarked in the bottom 10%. This instance is best suited for lightweight memory-intensive tasks, basic text processing, single-threaded scripting, or small-scale caching layers rather than high-throughput databases or parallelized compilation.

Operating on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features 1 physical core with 2 threads and dedicated CPU allocation, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core CPU profile (top 25% in stress-ng), contrasted by weak multi-core capabilities and poor memory bandwidth. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and text processing perform at average levels, whereas database operations and static web serving throughput fall into the bottom 10%. Qualitatively, the instance provides a cost-efficient entry point for memory-heavy, low-compute workloads. It is best suited for lightweight caching, single-threaded scripting, and basic text processing.
